learner_facing_text: Planned Foundation extension: arrive through the controlling check-in process, identify the person or process running the call, confirm the assigned department/work group, and report where directed; exact arrival timing and check-in procedure are call-specific.
notes: Final lesson placement deferred. Do not universalize one number of minutes early.

learner_facing_text: Planned Foundation extension: identify who owns your assignment and department; conflicting or changed instructions should go through the established call structure instead of silently self-reassigning or entering another department's technical work.
notes: Exact titles and chain of command vary by employer/local/production.

learner_facing_text: Planned Foundation extension: physical motion ending is not always assignment acceptance; compare the result to the requested state, report problems, hand control back to the responsible person when they own acceptance, and report back rather than disappearing from the task.
notes: Operationalizes existing Fundamentals and SFS-U05 handoff evidence.

learner_facing_text: Planned Foundation extension: when assigned work is actually complete, return to the established source of work and remain appropriately available for the next legitimate assignment rather than wandering into another department, inventing unauthorized work, or assuming the call is over.
notes: Captures the user's practical 'do the job, then downtime may happen' concept without teaching performative busyness or unauthorized work.

learner_facing_text: Planned Foundation extension: distinguish awaiting reassignment, production hold, standby/show waiting, an authorized short break, a meal period, and actual release; do not assume all downtime is a free break or all waiting is unpaid.
notes: Operational distinction is cross-source; legal compensation treatment requires correctly scoped employment/jurisdiction/CBA analysis.

learner_facing_text: Federal FLSA hours-worked examples apply only where the FLSA and the relevant covered employment relationship apply; employer practice, CBAs and state/local law may add or change obligations.
notes: Crew Blueprint is educational, not a payroll-law calculator.

learner_facing_text: Planned Foundation extension: show-call work has timing, presets, cues, changeovers, performer routes and show-critical boundaries; workers remain at the assigned place and available as directed rather than treating waiting or intermission as automatic release.
notes: Exact cue language, break practice, pay guarantees and continuity procedures remain production/CBA specific.

learner_facing_text: Planned Foundation extension: distinguish task done, department/work-group released, and call released; finishing one assignment does not by itself mean the worker may leave the call.
notes: Exact release/sign-out authority varies by call.

learner_facing_text: Planned Foundation extension: know and complete the controlling sign-in/sign-out/timecard/app/paperwork method accurately; physical departure does not necessarily create a correct time record, and discrepancies should go through the applicable payroll/steward/employer process.
notes: No single national timekeeping method is asserted.

learner_facing_text: Crew Blueprint should not assume every live-event worker has the same employee/contractor classification or that one federal recordkeeping rule resolves every state, local, contractual or payroll question.
notes: Conservative educational boundary for business/customer-facing content as well as curriculum.
